13 A vertical tube, closed at one end, is immersed in water. A column of air is trapped inside the
tube.
water surface
20.0 cm
water
air
30.0 cm
vertical tube
30.0 cm
The density of water is 1000 kg m–3.
What is the difference between the pressure of the air in the tube and the atmospheric pressure?
A
1960 Pa
B
2940 Pa
C
4910 Pa
D
7850 Pa

hints: Notice the horizontal dashed line at the bottom of the $30.0\text{ cm}$ air column - this is the air-water interface inside the tube.
Find how far that interface is below the outer water surface by adding the $20.0\text{ cm}$ water depth and the $30.0\text{ cm}$ air length.
Connect that depth $h$ to pressure difference with $\Delta p = \rho g h$ using $\rho = 1000\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and $h$ in metres.
walkthrough: Identify the level where inside and outside pressures can be compared: the air-water interface at the open bottom of the trapped air.
Measure its depth below the outer water surface from the diagram: $h = 20.0\text{ cm} + 30.0\text{ cm} = 50.0\text{ cm} = 0.50\text{ m}$.
State the hydrostatic rule: pressure increases with depth as $\Delta p = \rho g h$, so trapped air must be above atmospheric pressure by the pressure due to this water column.
Substitute values with units: $\Delta p = 1000\text{ kg m}^{-3} \times 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2} \times 0.50\text{ m}$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $\Delta p = 4905\text{ Pa}$, which rounds to $4910\text{ Pa}$ with a unit check of $\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2} = \text{Pa}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Uses only the $20.0\text{ cm}$ from the water surface to the top of the trapped air, not the depth to the air-water interface where pressures balance.

B.explanation: Uses only the $30.0\text{ cm}$ length of the trapped air column, not the total $50.0\text{ cm}$ depth of the air-water interface below the surface.

C.explanation: Equals $\rho g h$ with $h = 0.50\text{ m}$, the depth of the air-water interface below the surface, giving about $4910\text{ Pa}$.

D.explanation: Adds all three $20.0\text{ cm} + 30.0\text{ cm} + 30.0\text{ cm}$ lengths, but the lowest $30.0\text{ cm}$ is below the interface and does not affect the pressure difference.
